title: Days in a Month

concept.title: Putting small rules together
body: Bigger problems are built from small rules you already know. The length of a month follows a simple pattern: April, June, September and November have 30 days, February has 28 (or 29 in a leap year) and all other months have 31.

You already wrote the leap-year test in an earlier problem. Here it only matters for February, so it sits *inside* the branch for February. Always try to reuse a piece you have solved before instead of starting from scratch.
Grouping several exact values is easy with `or` (`||`), or in Python with `month in (4, 6, 9, 11)`.

statement: Given a month number (1 to 12) and a year, print the number of days in that month of that year.
A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 400, or if it is divisible by 4 but not by 100.
inputFormat: One line with two integers `month` and `year`.

examples.note: February in a leap year has 29 days.

hints: Which months have 30 days? Which one is special?
February needs the leap-year test: 29 days in a leap year, otherwise 28.
Every other month has 31 days, so it can be the final `else`.

starter.python:
month, year = map(int, input().split())
